hypotheses.reasoning: At 20:34:56, postgres reports a transaction (98979) from payment-svc-reconciler sitting idle in transaction while holding a RowExclusiveLock on "orders" (#104). Traffic was healthy until then. After that, UPDATEs on orders wait on that transaction's lock (#113, #119). payment-svc's /charge UPDATEs then hit the 10s statement timeout (#117, #127), and order-service's PaymentClient calls time out after 15s (#118, #128). Because calls were hanging, order-service's HTTP pool to payment-svc filled up (50/50, #133) and pool checkouts timed out (#142). The gateway then returned 504s on POST /checkout (#134 onward). Those are downstream symptoms. No deploy appears in the logs, and redis and the consumer look normal.
The payment-svc connection pool in order-service hit capacity. But it filled up only after the lock-induced timeouts started, so it's a symptom, not the trigger.

verdict.recommendedAction: Terminate the idle-in-transaction reconciler session: pg_terminate_backend on the backend for transaction 98979. Then fix payment-svc-reconciler so it commits or rolls back promptly instead of leaving transactions open. Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout on postgres for that role. Watch the order-service pool drain and the gateway 504 rate recover.
